metrics.name: Accessibility
metrics.description: Quality dimension implying that the KG is available, provides a public SPARQL endpoint, is retrievable in RDF format, supports content negotiation, and describes a licence.

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.description: Quality dimension defining the syntactic and semantic validity of assertions contained in the KG.

metrics.name: Appropriate amount
metrics.description: Quality dimension evaluating whether the KG contains knowledge for specific use case scenarios.

metrics.name: Believability or trustworthiness
metrics.description: Quality dimension measuring whether the KG provides provenance information and is verifiable.

metrics.name: Completeness
metrics.description: Quality dimension in terms of schema and instance level for a specific use case.

metrics.name: Concise representation
metrics.description: Quality dimension evaluating the use of blank nodes and reification.

metrics.name: Consistent representation
metrics.description: Quality dimension detecting the existence of disjoint inconsistencies of classes and schema restrictions in the KG.

metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness
metrics.description: Quality dimension measuring the degree to which accurate data is necessary.

metrics.name: Ease of manipulation
metrics.description: Quality dimension evaluating the existence of documentation for manipulating the knowledge contained in the KG.

metrics.name: Ease of operation
metrics.description: Quality dimension referring to the possibility of updating, downloading, and integrating the KG.

metrics.name: Ease of understanding
metrics.description: Quality dimension evaluating whether self-descriptive URIs are used and knowledge is presented in more than one language.

metrics.name: Free-of-error
metrics.description: Quality dimension referring to the total number of wrong and missing assertions contained in the KG.

metrics.name: Interoperability
metrics.description: Quality dimension evaluating whether the KG re-uses standard vocabularies and complies with Linked Open Data 5 Star.

metrics.name: Objectivity
metrics.description: Quality dimension defining the degree to which the KG is unbiased and impartial.

metrics.name: Relevancy
metrics.description: Quality dimension evaluating the level of applicability, in terms of domain coverage, of the KG to a specific use case.

metrics.name: Reputation
metrics.description: Quality dimension measuring whether explicit trust ratings exist to the KG or there exist qualifiers on KG’s statements.

metrics.name: Security
metrics.description: Quality dimension evaluating the degree to which the KG uses a digital signature and verifies the identity of the publisher.

metrics.name: Timeliness
metrics.description: Quality dimension measuring the frequency of updates occurring in the KG and the validity period of its statements.

metrics.name: Traceability
metrics.description: Quality dimension evaluating the degree to which the KG provides provenance information and keeps a log of edits and changes.

metrics.name: Variety
metrics.description: Quality dimension referring to the degree to which the KG contains knowledge from different sources and various domains.

concepts.name: Knowledge Graph Curation
concepts.description: The process of improving the quality of knowledge graphs.

concepts.name: Knowledge Graph Assessment
concepts.description: Evaluating the status and quality dimensions of knowledge graphs.

concepts.name: Knowledge Graph Cleaning
concepts.description: Tasks related to verification and validation of knowledge graphs.

concepts.name: Knowledge Graph Enrichment
concepts.description: Tasks related to detecting duplicates and knowledge fusion to improve completeness.

concepts.name: Verification
concepts.description: Evaluating KGs with formal specifications of integrity constraints.

concepts.name: Validation
concepts.description: Evaluating whether an assertion from a KG is semantically correct and corresponds with the real world.

concepts.name: Data Fusion
concepts.description: Resolving conflicting property value assertions from multiple records or KGs.

findings.name: Focus on specific tasks
findings.description: Most existing approaches and tools focus on one specific task, either assessing quality, detecting wrong assertions, or correcting them.

findings.name: Trade-off between completeness and correctness
findings.description: Curation of KGs usually implies a trade-off between correctness and completeness, and most approaches only detect errors or missing values leaving correction to users.

findings.name: Automation limits
findings.description: Various quality dimensions can hardly be fully automated for technical or operational reasons.

findings.name: Scalability limitations
findings.description: Existing frameworks still lack scalability to large knowledge graphs.

relationships.target: Resolving conflicting property value assertions or data fusion
